items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So he started telling me about the C7, B flat 7, F7. So he says, I'm going to buy you a record.

ctx.x: Joe Thomas was the alto player but he was Walter Foots Thomas' brother. And they had all been together down in Wichita. So they came and joined the Virginia Ravens. And then Merle left and a piano player out of Springfield, Missouri, I think that's right -- now, Springfield, Illinois, named Frank Hines. He took put Merle's place. And Frank was a marvelous piano player, he played something like Earl Hines. So we were with the Virginians and Frank used to say to me, "Eddie, you play a great jazz saxophone. But, he…
So he bought me a record of Frankie Trumbauer Trombaer singing the Blues." And I fell in love with that style so I started buying all the things that Frankie Trumbauer made, that he made
